task_context.problem_statement:
Lewis earns $ 491 every week during the 1181 weeks of harvest. If he has to pay $ 216 rent every week
How much money will have at the end of the harvest season?
( ( 491.0 - 216.0 ) * 1181.0 )

messages.content:
I have this problem: Lewis earns $ 491 every week during the 1181 weeks of harvest. If he has to pay $ 216 rent every week
How much money will have at the end of the harvest season?
( ( 491.0 - 216.0 ) * 1181.0 )

I honestly don't even know where to start. I'm so bad at word problems, I just can't do this.

It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed by word problems—they can be tricky because you have to translate words into math first. We can take this one step at a time. Let's ignore the total number of weeks for a moment. If Lewis earns $491 in a week but spends $216 on rent, how much does he actually keep for himself each week?
I guess I would subtract them? 491 minus 216... let me see... that's 275?
That's right. So, he saves $275 every single week. Now that we know his weekly savings, how do we figure out how much he has after all 1181 weeks of the harvest season?
Do I multiply the 275 by 1181? I'm probably going to mess up the multiplication though, I'm not great at big numbers.

Your logic is spot on! Multiplying the weekly savings by the number of weeks is exactly the right move. Don't worry about the size of the numbers—just take it slow, or use a piece of scratch paper to keep your columns straight. What do you get when you multiply 275 by 1181?
Okay, I tried it. I got 324,775. Is that actually right? I feel like it's too high.

You nailed it! 324,775 is the correct total. It seems like a huge number, but when you save a few hundred dollars every week for over a thousand weeks, it really adds up. You handled that perfectly, even the part you were worried about!
